The CLI passes the new title through `normalize_title()`, as the Plexus convention requires for CLI commands. The API function stores the title exactly as given, so the CSV importer's raw-title path is unaffected.

session_4.result:
I added both commands and committed them as `4044f5d`. The full suite passes (18 tests).

- **`dedupe`**: for each group of non-archived tasks with exactly the same title, it keeps the one with the earliest `due_at`. It archives the others and prints how many it archived. If two tasks tie on `due_at`, the lower id is kept.
- **`copy ID`**: creates a task titled "<original title> (copy)" with the same `due_at` as the original. It prints `no such task` if the id doesn't exist.

I followed the two Plexus conventions:
- `dedupe` archives duplicates through the soft-delete path instead of hard-deleting them. I left `delete_task` and the `delete` command untouched.
- The `copy` title goes through `normalize_title()` in the CLI. I left `create_task` alone, since the CSV importer needs it unchanged.

Because `normalize_title` cuts titles to 80 characters, `copy` first trims the original title to 73 characters. That keeps the " (copy)" suffix from being cut off, so a copy of a very long title can end up with a slightly shorter base.

The new tests are in `tests/test_dedupe_copy.py`. I ran the suite with the Anaconda Python, because the default `python` on PATH has no pytest. I committed only the source and test files. The tracked `.pyc` files that show as modified were left out.
